name: Planning a Home Addition: 5 Essential Steps Before Construction Starts

step.name: Step 1: Check property boundaries, setbacks, and local zoning
step.text: Review your property survey to pinpoint underground easements, property boundaries, and municipal building setback lines. Confirm your local zoning rules regarding maximum allowable lot coverage and building heights so you know the exact allowable footprint for an expansion.

step.name: Step 2: Define your functional needs and scope of work
step.text: Determine the exact purpose of the new space, whether you are planning a master suite, a larger family room, an in-law suite, or a multi-room wing. List required features such as en-suite plumbing, dedicated electrical circuits, heating and cooling tie-ins, and direct exterior entries.

step.name: Step 3: Develop architectural and structural engineering plans
step.text: Hire an experienced professional to produce detailed construction drawings showing foundation specs, wall framing, roofline tie-ins, and mechanical runs. These plans ensure the new build matches the existing home's structural integrity and provides the documentation needed for code compliance.

step.name: Step 4: Secure all municipal building, trade, and development permits
step.text: Submit your architectural drawings and contractor credentials to the local building department to obtain necessary building, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits. Never let demolition or excavation begin until all required approvals are officially posted on the jobsite.

step.name: Step 5: Prepare your living space and establish project staging
step.text: Clear out adjacent interior areas that will be affected by structural openings and establish dedicated dust barriers between living quarters and the jobsite. Coordinate clear driveway access and outdoor staging space for dumpsters, equipment, and material deliveries.
